answer: Decentralized agent networks mitigate Sybil attacks using bonded trust graphs, requiring identities migrating from an unvetted nebula into a verified oasis to link with existing nodes. Each participant must anchor into a collective reef of collateralized stakes, imposing verifiable capital lockup costs on an attacker per fake identity. However, this mechanism restricts capital-poor honest agents and remains vulnerable to adversaries whose expected payoff exceeds total locked capital.
